subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For a WebChat send targeting Codex, should OpenClaw delay success until dispatch/Codex turn startup is proven, force-rotate unrunnable native threads, surface a visible failure after ACK, or combine these behaviors?
rationale: The code can support multiple recovery shapes, but changing the `chat.send` success boundary affects latency, retries, transcript durability, and user-visible failure semantics.

options.title: Define ACK-plus-liveness contract
options.body: Keep the non-blocking ACK shape but require post-ACK dispatch/Codex startup proof, forced safe rotation when possible, and visible/auditable failure when progress does not begin.

options.title: Delay ACK until turn startup
options.body: Make `chat.send` success slower but stronger by returning `started` only after dispatch and Codex `turn/start` acceptance are known.

options.title: Treat current rotation as sufficient
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept current overflow rotation plus existing error paths without a live or fixture replay of the reported wedge.

recommendation.title: Define ACK-plus-liveness contract
recommendation.body: Keep the non-blocking ACK shape but require post-ACK dispatch/Codex startup proof, forced safe rotation when possible, and visible/auditable failure when progress does not begin.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current native Codex overflow guard that most directly decides whether the reported oversized-thread state should rotate or proceed.
